- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, creating a “peak then dip” pattern that doesn’t match true market behavior.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — it overreacts to recent volatility and fails to capture sustained trends.
- Forecast horizon 1–3 days shows high error, suggesting model lacks short-term calibration.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when prices are trending downward.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or event-driven price shifts (e.g., policy changes, emissions caps) — it treats all price movements as random.
- Model overweights recent history, leading to “recency bias” — it reacts too strongly to recent spikes or drops, ignoring longer-term trends.
- When true price rises sharply, model forecasts a higher peak than actual, then underestimates the subsequent decline.
- Model tends to underestimate the true price at the end of the forecast horizon — especially in downward trends — suggesting it lacks “tail risk” adjustment.
- Model does not account for lagged effects — it forecasts as if price changes are immediate, when in reality they often take 2–3 days to fully materialize.
